info.description:
The Credentials API provides a REST-ful API for managing Credentials, which are provided by a Principal,
that can then be used by other Flexera services to authenticate actions on behalf of that Principal.

## Organization vs. Project
The Credentials API can distinguish Credentials created at the Organization-level vs. Credentials created at the
Project-level. An Organization can have many Projects but it always has a primary Project.

The following rules apply to Credentials:
* An Organization can have a list of Credentials associated with it that can be used for Org-scoped actions.
* Any Project within that Organization can have its own list of Credentials that are scoped to actions specific to
  that Project. More specifically, any Credentials associated with the primary Project for an Organization are scoped
  to the primary Project and are kept separate from any Org-scoped Credentials associated with the Organization.
* Credentials are scoped to a particular Flexera Zone (see Endpoints below). For example, the list of
  Org-scoped Credentials for EU are distinct from the list of Org-scoped Credentials for APAC and
  are not addressable outside of that Zone. An Organization can logically span multiple Cloud-based regions
  (e.g. us-east-1 and us-west-2) by being associated with multiple Projects so long as those regions are supported by
  the same Flexera Zone (e.g. NAM).

## Endpoints
The API is available at the following endpoints, dependent upon the user/tenant zone:
| Zone | Scope        | Base URL                                  |
| ---- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| NAM  | Organization | https://api.flexera.com/cred/v2/orgs/     |
|      | Project      | https://api.flexera.com/cred/v2/projects/ |
| EU   | Organization | https://api.flexera.eu/cred/v2/orgs/      |
|      | Project      | https://api.flexera.eu/cred/v2/projects/  |
| APAC | Organization | https://api.flexera.au/cred/v2/orgs/      |
|      | Project      | https://api.flexera.au/cred/v2/projects/  |

tags.description:
API Key supports signing requests using a pre-defined header or query parameter that
does not change unless updated by a Principal.
tags.name: API Key Credential

tags.description:
AWS supports signing requests using
[AWS Signature Version 4](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-auth-using-authorization-header.html).
The AWS Access Key ID and Secret Key will remain the same until updated by a Principal.
tags.name: AWS Credential

tags.description:
AWS STS supports signing requests using
[AWS Signature Version 4](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-auth-using-authorization-header.html).
A temporary session token will be acquired and used for signing. For this the Principal provides a Role ARN and an
External ID that is then used to assume a role via the
[AWS Security Token Service Assume Role API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html).
The Role ARN provided by the Principal must refer to an AWS Role that has been configured to trust the AWS Role ARN
that is provided by Flexera.

References:
* [Flexera Automation](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Automation/ProviderCredentials.htm)
* [Flexera CCO](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/OptimaBillConnectConfigsAWSConfigAccess.htm)

Note that other Flexera services may have additional documentation for use of AWS STS Credentials.
tags.name: AWS STS Credential

tags.description:
Basic supports signing requests using
[Basic Authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication).
A user name and password are required and they do not change unless updated by a Principal.
tags.name: Basic Credential

tags.description: The Credential service supports actions that do not require specific Credential media types or payload.
tags.name: Credential

tags.description:
Digest supports signing requests using
[Digest Authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digest_access_authentication).
A user name and password are required and they do not change unless updated by a Principal.
The URL must refer to a host that supports Digest Authentication.
tags.name: Digest Credential

tags.description:
NTLM supports signing requests using
[NTLM Authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTLM).
A user name and password are required and they do not change unless updated by a Principal.
tags.name: NTLM Credential

tags.description:
NTLM supports signing requests using [OAuth2 Authentication](https://oauth.net/2/).
There are multiple accepted forms of OAuth2 but this service supports the "client-credentials", "jwt-bearer" and
"refresh-token" grant types. In all cases a temporary access token is retrieved from the OAuth2 host and used to
sign requests.
tags.name: OAuth2 Credential

tags.description:
Oracle supports signing requests using
[Oracle API Key-Based Authentication](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
An application may also be able to use OAuth2 for calls to Oracle services but this proprietary algorithm is still
supported for historical reasons.
tags.name: Oracle Credential
